summary: Adolf Noreen was a linguist who studied at Uppsala University (~1871–1877) and under August Leskien (~1879). He subsequently held a post at Uppsala University from circa 1877 to 1919.

Adolf Schlagintweit was a medical doctor and archaeologist/historian who earned his Dr.med. at the University of Munich (~1846–1849). He served there as Privatdozent in 1850 and was employed by the East India Company for exploration in 1854.

Linguist Adolf Tobler studied at the University of Zurich (~1853–1854) and the University of Bonn (~1854–1857) under Friedrich Christian Diez and Nikolaus Delius. He held a position at the Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1867 to 1910.

Adolfo Esteller y Melià was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, Ignatius College, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders and Wilhelm Schulze. He later served as professor and director at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1937–1964).
Linguist Adolphe Pictet studied at Geneva, Paris, Berlin (under G. W. F. Hegel, 1821–1823), Edinburgh, and London. He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Geneva between 1840 and 1844.

Adolphe Regnier was an Indologist, linguist, and historian who studied under Eugène Burnouf (1835–1838). He taught at Lycée Saint-Louis, Lycée Charlemagne, Collège de France (1838–1843), and École Normale Supérieure, later joining the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1855).

Adoniram Judson Eaton was an Indologist and linguist educated at Acadia, Harvard, Yale, and the University of Leipzig (Ph.D. ~1882–1884). He served as Principal of Woonsocket High School (~1876–1882) and Associate Professor of Classics at McGill University (1886).

Indologist Adriaan Scharpé studied at KU Leuven and Utrecht University, completing his Ph.D. under Jan Gonda. He served as a docent at Ghent University (1944–1979) and extraordinary professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Indo-European at the University of Amsterdam (1947–1978).

Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. After studying at the University of Auckland and the University of Cambridge, he taught at the European School of Culture and Theology (~2007–2018) and became a Senior Fellow at the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation (2019).

Adrien Barthélemy worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at INALCO and under James Darmesteter at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1880–1884), he served as directeur d’études at the EPHE and taught at INALCO from 1909 to 1929.

Adrienne Audrey G. Bennett worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She served as librarian for the Buddhist Society (1949–1952), edited The Middle Way (1951–1952), and held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society (1956–1966).

Adrián Muñoz works in Indology and religious studies. He has served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (attested 2011) and as a lecturer of South Asian Religions at El Colegio de México (attested 2020).

Afeef Ahmed works in Indology and history/archaeology. He held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar and became a graduate student and Ph.D. candidate in South Asian Studies at Harvard University (attested 2024–2026).

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and University of Bonn (1995), and holds an affiliation with the University of Warsaw (attested 2008, 2026).

Agathe Keller works in Indology and history/archaeology. After earning her Ph.D. and habilitation at Paris Diderot University (2000), she held posts with REHSEIS, Paris Diderot University, and the CNRS, serving as a DR2 researcher there in 2005.

Agehananda Bharati was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Vienna and Sannyasi Mahavidyalaya. He taught at Banaras Hindu University (1951–1954) and held posts at the University of Washington (1957–1961) and Syracuse University (1961–1991).
Agnes Margrethe Agerschou was an Indologist and linguist who completed her M.A. at the University of Copenhagen by 1940. She served as an assistant for the Critical Pāli Dictionary from 1940 to 1949.

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw and Nicolaus Copernicus University (Ph.D. 2007), later holding posts at Cornell (~2008–2010), the University of Warsaw (2015), and the University of Hamburg (2015).

Agvan Dorzhiev was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery, attaining the Geshe Lharampa degree. He taught the 13th Dalai Lama and founded the Atsagat Datsan (1913) and Datsan Gunzechoinei.

Ahmad Hasan Dani was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of London. He headed the Department of Archaeology at the University of Peshawar (1962–1971) and later served as Dean at Quaid-i-Azam University (1971).
